tagline: Linux paths and hardware bridges for Xios
description:
**xios-fhs** sets up the standard Linux filesystem paths the Xios desktop expects, plus small daemons that expose iPad hardware to Linux apps: battery and backlight through **xios-hwbridged**, and the motion sensors through **xios-sensord** (an iio-sensor-proxy stand-in, used by GNOME for auto-rotate).

You normally don't install this directly. The Xios desktop flavors pull it in.

changelog.notes:
- xios-sensord now reads the motion sensors only while an app asks for them, and writes a value only when it changes
- Before this, it polled the sensors ten times a second around the clock and rewrote nine files on every poll, syncing each one to flash. On my iPad that was about 29 GB of flash writes a day and a fifth of a CPU core, even with no desktop running
- Sensor claims are now tracked per app, so an app that crashes no longer leaves a sensor running
